messages:
Sam: quick overnight handoff — coverage 18:00-06:00 PT. Main watchlist items below, please ack and note if you take a shift.

Sam: 1) eu-prefix-cache: noisy alerts started cropping up ~2h ago, alert bursts every ~5-10m, looks like duplicate detection flapping. Metrics: high prefix-cache-misses + alert debounce firing. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefix-cache-noise (check consumer backpressure, log sampling).
Sam: 2) kv-pool-ttl: slow memory creep in pool swapper, non-incident but trending. Watch pool_free_bytes and eviction_rate.
Sam: 3) encoder-pool (p3-dedicated): p95 latency drift after a small autoscale tweak this morning. Not yet user-impacting but keep an eye on regen failures >0.3%.

Marta: ack — I can take 18:00-00:00. Will start by throttling alert channel (mute temporary) and add a verbose log snapshot to the runbook.

Alex: @Marta thanks. If you see repeated bursts, try increasing the alert debounce from 30s->90s in alert-config for eu (safe for now). I pushed a draft change in infra-config PR #821.

Jess: FYI I rolled a tiny encoder autoscaler tweak at 09:15; saw slight p95 bump but error rates stayed flat. Reverting would be easy if it spikes.

Ryan: ping on my PR #421 (kv-pool telemetry) — it adds an extra gauge for pool_free_bytes per shard which should help root cause. Can one of you review?

Marta: will review PR #421 after handoff, ETA ~19:00. Also will run the `kv-diagnostics` snippet if memory climb continues:
```
# quick snapshot
curl -sS http://metrics.local/kv/pools | jq '.pools[] | {name, free_bytes, evictions}'
```

Alex: noted on debounce tweak. If we change debounce, let's add a short note in the alert description so paging teams understand.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled rotation in 11h. If you need to swap, post here and tag @eng-oncall.

oncall-bot: Incident-free for 72 hours — keep monitoring thresholds.

Jess: small heads-up — I saw one trace with encoder OOM last night in staging, might be unrelated but worth keeping an eye on p3 node memory.

Marta: taking point on noisy-alert triage. If I can't stabilize within 30m, I'll escalate to Eng Runtime (tagging @alex).

Alex: available if needed, ping me with trace IDs.

Ryan: ack — I'll skim telemetry and leave notes on PR.

Marta: leaving detailed handoff in pager duty note once I start shift. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
